label: caiso 10 baseline anchor
definition: WHERE-ARE-WE ANCHOR: the caiso-9 keeper config (RA must-offer gas floor 0.80x EIA-930 NG:NG + negative-renewable-offers, both ON by default; priced interchange; 2025 hydro repinned to EIA-930) re-solved on current main to confirm no code drift. Mix is in tolerance vs the right benchmarks: 2024 gas 70.9 vs EIA-923 67.7 (+4.8%, mild floor inflation), wind/solar/hydro match EIA-930. THE open structural error is the LMP floor: min $0.00 and 0 negative hours all 3 yrs (2024 avg $54.2 vs actual RT ~$33; actual min ~-$58). Root cause is visible in the interchange: imports are far too FLAT — they never back off midday so the model is never long enough to price its surplus at/below $0. Import diurnal swing model vs actual: 2023 1662/5236, 2024 1492/4596, 2025 725/4973 MW; import-hours 97.9/96.4/99.9% vs actual 85.9/89.0/90.9%. Model never exports the midday glut. Secondary: 2023 over-import +10.6 TWh (cheap-gas year, static tranche prices < $2.54 HH). NEXT: caiso-11 adds --interchange-shaping (export the midday glut) — the missing key that, once the export sink saturates, forces surplus to curtail renewables at -$20 and unlock the negative tail.
